summary_html: Case dismissed due to **unsubstantiated evidence** or court determination that allegations not proven. Federal oversight requires accurate recording of such closures for audit and funding compliance.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — defines data-collection standards for unfounded cases  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — requires tracking and reporting of unsubstantiated outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: Oklahoma - Title 10A (Children and Juvenile Code), § 1-2-101 (Duty to report) and Article 1, Part 4 (deprived child proceedings)
Title 10a: Children and Juvenile Code - CHILD WELFARE PRIMARY

regulations_applicable.title: Title 135 - Commission on Children and Youth

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the termination of an incarcerated father's parental rights because the record contained no clear and convincing evidence supporting the statutory grounds alleged against him.
key_cases.relevance: The reversal ends the State's termination case against this parent for want of proof.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the record does not include clear and convincing evidence supporting termination in this case and reverse.

key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a deprived adjudication, holding the State could re-remove and refile after the first case failed for want of a petition within seven days, that holding the emergency custody hearing on the third judicial day violated the two-day rule but did not divest jurisdiction or deny due process, and that competent evidence supported the adjudication.
key_cases.relevance: The first deprived case was dismissed and the child returned solely because the State missed the filing deadline.
key_cases.quote: The burden of proof is on the State to demonstrate the factual basis for the deprived status adjudication by a preponderance of the evidence.

key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma
key_cases.holding: The court vacated a deprived adjudication as to a father because the trial court treated the mother's no-contest stipulation as binding on him and denied the non-jury trial he requested, and remanded for a trial meeting ICWA standards.
key_cases.relevance: The adjudication as to the father was vacated outright, returning his part of the case to square one.
key_cases.quote: We therefore find that the trial court committed reversible error in denying Father's request for a non-jury trial

extended_foster_care_age: Up to age 21 (voluntary; conditions apply; began 1 July 2026; 10A O.S. § 1-7-112a)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.deadline: 6 months, then every 6 months thereafter; 30 days after a court determination that reasonable efforts to return the child are not required
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Child enters out-of-home placement — the earlier of the adjudication date or 60 days after the child is removed from the home

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
